lesson.title: Room, Brood & Bellen
lesson.subtitle: the traps that look like English

hook.title: Lookalikes Are Not Twins
hook.content: Room is cream, brood is bread, bellen is to phone. The words look English but mean something else. The Dutch twin of the English word is usually a different word entirely.

pattern.title: Check the meaning, not the shape
pattern.content: Room looks like room but means cream; the room is kamer. Brood looks like brood but means bread. Bellen looks like bell but means to phone. When a Dutch word looks too English, slow down.
pattern.trap_note: Dier looks like deer but means any animal; a deer is hert. Meer looks like mere but means lake (and also more).

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Room, Brood & Bellen):
exercises.target_answer: de room, het brood, bellen, het vuur, het dier, meer
exercises.meaning: cream, bread, to call, phone, fire, animal, more; lake
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Room, Brood & Bellen": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “The cream is cold.”?
exercises.explanation: “De room is koud.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Room, Brood & Bellen”.

cues: The pattern: Check the meaning, not the shape
It means: The bread is fresh.
exercises.explanation: “Het brood is vers.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Check the meaning, not the shape.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Dier looks like deer but means any animal; a deer is hert. Meer looks like mere but means lake (and also more).

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Ik bel mijn moeder.” is word-for-word “I bell my mother.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Check the meaning, not the shape.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: The animal is big.
exercises.explanation: “Het dier is groot.” reuses only material taught in “Room, Brood & Bellen” — Check the meaning, not the shape.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Het dier is groot.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Check the meaning, not the shape.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “The lake is cold.”
twist.explanation: Meer can mean 'more' or 'lake'; here the article het and the context make it a lake.

summary.outcome: Recognise six high-frequency false friends and recall their real meanings.
summary.takeaway: A false friend is a word whose shape lies; check the meaning before you translate.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Jij, U & Doe Normaal.

room.etymology_derivation: English room is unrelated; Dutch room is cream.

brood.etymology_derivation: English bread and Dutch brood are the same word with different vowels.

bellen.etymology_derivation: From the bell used to call; Dutch turned it into the everyday phone verb.

vuur.etymology_derivation: English fire and Dutch vuur are cognate; f voiced to v.

dier.etymology_derivation: English deer narrowed the meaning to one species; Dutch kept 'animal'.

meer.etymology_derivation: English more and Dutch meer are the same word; het meer also means lake.
